# Independent review of the field generated by a normalized coefficient

## Whole finding

At 2026-11-22T04:18 UTC a reviewer acting for Yin independently checked the statement and all three proof sections of C_A0116_v1, including the reduction of arbitrary two-by-two matrices and the finite tracial comparison.
The reviewer took no part in developing the argument, received its fixed text and the scope of the assignment, and consulted the inverse-layer definition and the cited direct-sum construction with its source inspection.
The reviewer received no proof-development dialogue or prior review verdict about this Claim.
The hypotheses now explicitly identify the scalar unit condition and the layer containing the four entries in the three-dimensional case.
The whole conditional statement is supported, with the group case of the mixed product left open.

For every complex \(\lambda\), independence gives \(a\ne0\) and \(b-\lambda a\ne0\).
Their inverses therefore occur among the generators of \(D_{k+1}(G)\).
Multiplication in both orders verifies \((x-\lambda)^{-1}=(b-\lambda a)^{-1}a\).
For a polynomial \(q(t)=c\prod_i(t-\lambda_i)\) with \(c\ne0\), the factors and their inverses commute as functions of \(x\), so \(q(x)^{-1}=c^{-1}\prod_i\bigl((b-\lambda_i a)^{-1}a\bigr)\).
This covers repeated roots and constants, proves injectivity on polynomials, and puts every fraction with nonzero denominator in the same layer.

For \(p=ah\ne0\) with \(h\) in the resulting field \(F\), \(p^{-1}=h^{-1}a^{-1}\) belongs to \(D_{k+1}(G)\).
The middle factors \(a^{-1}a\) in the Schur update cancel in this order, leaving an element of \(aF\).
For an \(m\times n\) matrix, removal of the left factor amounts to the range automorphism \(\operatorname{diag}_m(a^{-1})\) of the affiliated right module \(U^m\).
Field row and column operations give a rectangular identity block of size \(r\) with zero complement.
All these operations preserve the module dimension of the image, which is \(r\) under the ordinary unnormalized matrix trace.
An independent basis of a two-dimensional entry span gives affine polynomials after normalization, and in dimension one a single nonzero entry suffices to obtain a constant matrix.
The zero matrix has rank zero.
At size two, eliminating a nonzero leading entry leaves one scalar pivot whose rank is one precisely when the commutative determinant of the normalized matrix is nonzero.

For \(N=PMQ\), substitution of \(M=P^{-1}NQ^{-1}\) into the coefficient pairing gives the coefficient of \(N_{uv}\) as \(\sum_{ij}(P^{-1})_{iu}K_{ij}(Q^{-1})_{vj}\).
Thus the relation transforms as \(P^{-t}KQ^{-t}\) without permuting any operator factors.
These two constant changes preserve the dimension of the entry span and the operator rank.
A rank-one relation can be moved to a lower-left coordinate, where that entry vanishes and the other three are independent.
The resulting triangular matrix has two affiliated units on its diagonal, hence rank two.
For invertible \(K\) one can take \(P=K^t\) and \(Q=I\), producing the relation \(N_{11}+N_{22}=0\).
Dimension three forces the remaining coefficients \(a,b,c\) to be independent.
Eliminating the unit pivot in the normalized matrix produces \(-1-yx\), with \(y=a^{-1}c\) on the left and \(x=a^{-1}b\) on the right.
This proves precisely the rank formula \(1+\operatorname{rk}(1+yx)\).

If any original entry is zero, permutations put it below the diagonal.
Two nonzero diagonal entries are units, while a triangular matrix with a zero on its diagonal has only one potentially nonzero row or column.
Such a matrix has rank one whenever a nonzero scalar entry is present and has rank zero otherwise.
For the remaining matrices the indicated diagonal multiplications give the four entries \(da,dba,-c,-da\) in that order, all still in \(D_k(G)\).
The multipliers \(d,a\) are affiliated units.
The entries are therefore contained in the span of \(p=da,u=dba,v=-c\).
Dependence gives integer rank by the two-coefficient result.
Independence reduces the rank to the mixed scalar expression above, and every independent triple occurs by choosing the matrix with entries \(p,u,v,-p\) itself.
For \(a,d\ne0\), substituting \((da)^{-1}=a^{-1}d^{-1}\) gives the stronger identity \(1+(p^{-1}v)(p^{-1}u)=a^{-1}d^{-1}(d-ca^{-1}b)a\), verifying equality of scalar ranks.
Because the group trace is faithful and normalized, integral scalar rank is equivalent to zero or full rank.
This establishes both directions at the same original layer \(k\).

In the ledger construction the triple \(Y\) is algebraically free and has integer polynomial-matrix rank, so a nonzero scalar polynomial has rank one on \(Y\).
The free semicircular triple \(Z\) preserves polynomial inner rank, giving the same scalar conclusion.
For the symmetric two-by-two test, the matrix on \(Y\) is reduced by diagonal multiplications by \(T^{-1}\) to \((1,S)^t(1,S)\) of rank one.
On \(Z\), the formal matrix has inner rank two because the specialization \((1,0,1)\) gives the identity.
The average trace therefore gives rank \(3/2\).
The stated right multiplication sends the rows to \((X_2,-X_1),(X_3,-X_2)\), with \(X_2\) an affiliated unit by scalar injectivity and finite trace.
Subtracting its pivot rank gives \(1/2\) for the ordered product expression in the Claim.
The ledger and MSY23 source unit supply the stated inputs at the indicated scope.
This comparison tests finite tracial representations of the polynomial algebra and leaves regular group convolution unresolved.
